title: Djokovic Wins First Match Since Wimbledon at China Open
summary:
Novak Djokovic is back! The 39-year-old tennis star beat Nuno Borges at the China Open on Wednesday for his first win since reaching the Wimbledon semi-finals in July. He won 6-3, 7-6 (7-2).

It wasn't easy. Djokovic struggled in the second set. He used his racquet to stretch his back between games and needed a medical timeout for his right shoulder. He also revealed in August that he has an underlying health condition that bothers him in hot, humid weather. But he battled for one hour and 50 minutes to win.

This was Djokovic's first time at the China Open since 2015. He now has 30 straight victories in Beijing — an amazing record. He's a 24-time Grand Slam champion and is trying to win the China Open for a record seventh time. Next, he faces wildcard Bu Yunchaokete of China.

In the women's draw, Great Britain's Katie Boulter also moved on. She beat Mai Hontama of Japan 6-3, 6-4 and will face Czech seventh seed Karolina Muchova next.
why_it_matters: Even champions get hurt and have tough days, so Djokovic's win is a reminder that asking for help, taking a break and refusing to give up can matter just as much as talent.

background_read: Novak Djokovic (a Serbian tennis player who has won more Grand Slam titles than any other man) has been one of the world's top players for almost twenty years.

The China Open is a tennis tournament played in Beijing, China each autumn, and Wimbledon (the oldest and most famous tennis tournament, played on grass in London) is the one every player dreams of winning.
Tennis matches can last for hours, so players are allowed a short medical timeout, when a doctor or trainer can check an injury.

WHAT: Djokovic won his first match since July's Wimbledon semi-finals, beating Borges 6-3, 7-6 (7-2) in one hour and 50 minutes.
WHERE: The China Open in Beijing, China — his first time at the tournament since 2015.
WHY: He is trying to win the China Open a record seventh time, despite a right shoulder problem and a health condition that makes hot, humid weather hard for him.

perspectives.description: They are thrilled that he is back on court and winning again, and they believe he can still add more titles to his record.
Some worry that playing long matches in very hot, humid weather can be risky, especially for players who already have a health condition.
